Below is a concise recap with recommended model variants, quick Redwood-verified performance highlights, and proposed next steps so your infra/security teams can evaluate scope. I attached the CSV of the verified profiles and a small prompt pack we used for the benchmark.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Recommended shortlist: nimblesurf-13b-q4 (quantized) and nimblesurf-7b-fp16 for latency-sensitive paths.
- Verified throughput/latency (internal lab, 1xA10): nimblesurf-13b-q4: peak steady TPS 420, p50 latency 92ms, p95 260ms; nimblesurf-7b-fp16: peak TPS 980, p50 45ms, p95 120ms.
- Quality note: on your intent classification prompt set we saw ~1.8% drop vs. the 13b fp baseline for the 13b quantized variant on long-context (>1024 tokens) examples; recommend regression guardrails (prompt-length caps + prefix caching).

Artifacts attached/shared
- redwood-verified-profiles-clearbridge.csv (per-model TPS, p50/p95/p99 traces)
- prompt-set-customer-intents-v1.md (30 representative prompts used for quality checks)

- Drive: https://drive.redwood.company/Shared/CLB-eval/2028-09-17/index.html (dashboards + raw traces)

Engineer notes (quick) — Karthik, feel free to expand below if I missed anything important for their security/ops folks.

Model selection rationale
- nimblesurf-13b-q4: best balance for your high-accuracy conversational intents when latency can tolerate ~100–250ms p50–p95. Q4 quantization saves ~2.8x memory vs fp16 and matches top-line accuracy on short contexts.
- nimblesurf-7b-fp16: lower-cost path for high-throughput classification or short-response generation. Good fit for ephemeral scoring and front-door filtering.

Operational recommendations
- Enable prefix/KV caching for flows with repeated system/context tokens — you should see 20–40% token cost reduction on steady state.
- Start pilot on Dedicated single-tenant nodes to lock SLOs (we can set autoscale caps) and enable trace-forwarding to your SIEM.

Proposed next steps
1) Share this email and attachments with your security + procurement.
2) Karthik and Marissa to provide short answers to the security checklist and an SLO sketch by EOD Wed (20 Sep).
3) If green, schedule a 2-week pilot window (we recommended 30 Sept start) — I can provision a pilot cluster and upload the short traces.

Looking forward to your questions.

Sequence lengths for quoted numbers
- The 13b-q4 p95 datapoint (260ms) is from a mixed workload with 60% 512-token, 30% 1k-token, 10% 2.5k-token requests (single A10 with our continuous-batching runtime). For a workload skewed to 1.5k tokens the p95 increases to ~420ms in our tests; p50 moves to ~140ms.

Pilot TCO rough order (2-week run, Dedicated, mid-latency SLOs)
- For 5k sustained QPS ephemeral scoring this would require a multi-node Dedicated cluster. Rough estimate (including bandwidth and storage for traces): $125k–$185k for a 2-week reserved pilot footprint (we can provide a cost-optimized config with autoscale/burst controls to lower run-rate). I can produce a tighter projection if you share expected average tokens per request.

Quality/regression guardrails
- Two practical steps to reduce degradation risk when using quantized variants: 1) enforce a max-context truncation at 2048 for the pilot; 2) add a regression checklist that runs the prompt-set-customer-intents-v1.md suite on any model flip. We can wire this into Redwood Optimize so you get automatic alerts when quality drifts >1% on key intents.

Security/compliance notes
